newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daiwa, Yamaichi provided profit to sokaiya - paper.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa, Yamaichi provided profit to sokaiya - paper.

text.p: Daiwa Securities Co Ltd and Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd provided a total of 280 million yen to a "sokaiya" racketeer in illicit deals, the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Wednesday.
Spokesmen for Daiwa and Yamaichi were not immediately available for comment on the report.
The paper said Nikko Securities Co Ltd may also have made illegal deals for sokaiya Ryuichi Koike, who is a key figure in the high-profile payoff scandal.

Prosecutors and the securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), plan to investigate the deals at the three firms for alleged violations of securities and commercial laws, the paper said.
The paper quoted unspecified sources as saying Daiwa provided about 200 million yen to Koike around 1993 to offset some of his losses stemming from stock transactions.
Yamaichi provided Koike with 80 million yen, which it made through deals on SIMEX in 1995, to offset stock trading losses, the sources were quoted as saying.
Other papers also reported on Wednesday that Yamaichi provided 80 million yen to Koike.
